_comment: Design-coverage divergences for wedding-planner (Everly). Each entry records where the Stitch design's heading is deliberately NOT copied verbatim because it is sample data the app renders from its own records, or a feature/cclaim the template does not ship. Sections themselves are implemented; only the sample-data names / unshipped features are allowlisted. Reviewed 2026-09-28.

allow.heading: Clara Vance & Julian Hastings
allow.reason: Sample couple names in the design; the page renders the wedding's real partner names from the couple's own record ({{a}} & {{b}} are getting married).

allow.heading: The Harrington Household
allow.reason: Sample household/Party name in the design; guests are looked up by their own name from the couple's guest list, not a fixed household.

allow.heading: Everything for your journey to Sovicille
allow.reason: Design's travel-notes heading names the sample venue's town; the implemented 'Celebration Details & Travel Notes' section carries the evergreen 'Everything for your journey' subtitle since the venue is per-wedding data.

allow.heading: Attendance Confirmation
allow.reason: Implemented verbatim as the respond-step heading; it appears after a guest finds their name, while the rendered audit navigates the literal '/rsvp/:code' URL which shows the code-not-found screen.

allow.heading: Dinner & Culinary Selections
allow.reason: Implemented verbatim above the meal selector in the respond step; hidden behind name lookup (by design — guests must identify themselves first), which the audit's literal ':code' navigation never reaches.

allow.heading: Celebration Details & Travel Notes
allow.reason: Implemented verbatim on the lookup step; the audit's literal ':code' URL renders the not-found screen instead of a real wedding.

allow.heading: Good morning, Clara & Julian
allow.reason: The headline renders a real time-of-day greeting (good morning/afternoon/evening) with the wedding's actual partner names — 'Clara & Julian' is the design's sample couple.

allow.heading: Marcus Harrington
allow.reason: Sample guest name in the design; the table renders the couple's real guest rows from their own seeded/entered data.

allow.heading: Villa Cetinale Estate
allow.reason: Sample vendor name (design's venue); the app renders its own seeded vendor records (e.g. Linden Hall Estate) and user-entered vendors.

allow.heading: Chianti Vineyards Catering & Banquets
allow.reason: Sample vendor name (design's caterer); the app renders its own seeded catering vendor records.

allow.heading: Matteo V. Visuals & Film
allow.reason: Sample vendor name (design's photographer); the app renders its own seeded photography vendor records.

allow.reason: Sample vendor name (design's florist); the app renders its own seeded floral vendor records.

allow.heading: Siena Candle & Atmospheric Lighting
allow.reason: Sample vendor name (design's lighting supplier); lighting vendors appear under Floral Architecture & Scenography / Other artisans when the couple adds them.

allow.heading: Chianti Bridal Atelier (Elena S.)

allow.reason: title-case divergence only: the section is implemented ('Needs immediate attention') and lists overdue tasks; the static gate matched on word overlap so no suppression is needed, recorded here for rendered-audit traceability.

allow.reason: Sample task title in the design; the sections render the couple's real seeded/entered tasks (e.g. 'Book caterer + menu tasting').

allow.reason: Sample task title in the design; tasks render from the couple's own checklist.

allow.reason: Sample table name; tables render from the couple's own records.

allow.reason: Sample table name; tables render from the couple's own records.

allow.heading: Table 03: Olive Grove

allow.heading: Notification Cadence & Peaceful Digests
allow.reason: Implemented verbatim as the Notifications panel heading; it renders inside that tab's panel, which is not mounted until the tab is opened (the audit never clicks tabs).

allow.heading: Subscription & Atelier Plan
allow.reason: Implemented as the Subscription panel heading ('Subscription & Atelier plan'); renders inside the tab panel, not on the default Profile tab paint.

allow.heading: Danger Zone & Archive Safeguards
allow.reason: Implemented as the danger-zone card heading inside the Subscription panel with the real cancel-plan action; renders inside the tab panel, not on initial paint.

allow.heading: Shared Partner & Planner Co-Access
allow.reason: The template's account model is single-owner (one login per wedding suite); a partner/planner co-access invite flow is not implemented, so no such section is faked.

allow.heading: Security & Passkey
allow.reason: The template ships password auth only (change-password form lives in the Security panel); no passkey/2FA management exists in the API, so the design's passkey framing is not claimed.

allow.heading: Artisan & Vendor Contract Vault
allow.reason: No contract escrow/vault feature exists in the template; the implemented next-steps grid only names real destinations (guest list, seating studio, vendor pipeline, budget tracker).

allow.heading: Dedicated Tuscan Concierge Sync
allow.reason: No concierge/messaging feature exists in the template; not claimed.

allow.heading: Interactive 3D Seating Studio
allow.reason: The seating studio is 2D; the card is titled 'Interactive seating studio' to stay factual, and the design's '3D' wording is not claimed.

allow.heading: Immediate Next Steps in Your Suite
allow.reason: title-case divergence only: implemented as 'Immediate next steps in your suite'; recorded here for rendered-audit traceability.

allow.heading: 256-Bit Protection
allow.reason: Design badge makes a specific cryptography claim the template cannot verify; the page states what is true instead (TLS in transit, salted-hashed passwords, single-use reset code) and the badge is not copied.
